elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly permits Company to terminate “this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires “thirty (30) days advance” notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly requires “written notice to Contractor.”

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees following Customer's termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph provides that “Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees” upon such termination.

elements.element: The refund of prepaid fees must be calculated pro rata for the period after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: The refund applies “pro rata for the period after the effective date of such termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Contractor may not terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience “while any Statement of Work is outstanding,” and existing subsection (a) permits termination only when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding.
The added paragraph expressly grants Company a termination-for-convenience right for the Agreement or any Statement of Work.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, which is below the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee for Customer's convenience termination must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; instead, Contractor must refund prepaid fees pro rata.
Existing subsection (a) permits “either party” to terminate for any or no reason when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor's right is triggered whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, not expressly only at the scheduled end of an Agreement or renewal term. The Agreement itself continues until terminated and has no defined end-of-term trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Existing subsection (a) permits Vendor termination on only fifteen (15) days' advance notice.

result.reason: The added operative language fully implements the preferred position: Company receives a 30-day written convenience-termination right, prepaid fees are refunded pro rata, and Contractor cannot terminate while a Statement of Work is outstanding. The changes are targeted and leave the unrelated breach-termination provisions intact. The fallback is not independently satisfied because Company's notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days, and Contractor retains a 15-day right that is not expressly limited to an end-of-term event.
